topic.title: Adversarial Examples and Multimodal Defense
topic.overview: Adversarial inputs deliberately exploit a model’s sensitivities to alter its behavior. This topic studies attacks and defenses across images, speech, structured prediction, and vision-language systems, including visual prompt injection. Methods differ in available access, query budgets, perturbation constraints, and the task outcome they attempt to change.
topic.whyItMatters: Robustness claims are meaningful only relative to a specified threat model and evaluation. A defense that handles familiar perturbations may fail against an adaptive adversary, while aggregate success rates can obscure utility losses. Studying attacks provides a way to test these boundaries systematically.
topic.evolution: Houdini in 2017 targets task-level performance measures for structured outputs. Later representatives explore limited-query attacks, visible patches, adversarial training, and generative purification. A 2026 visual-injection defense uses hidden-state gradient attribution to identify and suppress critical image tokens, reporting strong protection within its tested multimodal attack settings.
openQuestions: How can defenses remain effective when attackers adapt to the defense itself?
Which evaluations jointly measure preserved task utility and resistance to multimodal manipulation?
